And in the year 1450 {Greek},
and he conquered two fortresses, Bahgai and Gabnupirat.
And he also invaded the region of Kasinos, which is on the coast of the sea of Pontus,
and pillaged and took captive all the people,
and sold them into slavery.
And in the year
1451 of the Greeks [1139/1140 AD]:
The earth split open in the region of Kalonikos,
and swallowed forty horsemen along with their horses;
and only one, who had turned aside to urinate, was saved.
And the sound of the cries of the people and their horses kept rising up for a long time.
And in the year
534 of the Arabs [1139/1140 AD]:
The word of Sultan Mas'ud, which he spoke to the vizier Sharaf al-Din,
that he had erred in the election of the Caliph, was fulfilled.
For that Caliph began to manage political affairs without the advice of the vizier,
and the vizier was confined to his house.
And when he summoned him,
he was reconciled with him in an insincere reconciliation.
And the hand of the vizier was restricted from many affairs,
and after a little while he dismissed him completely from the vizierate.
And in the year
535 (in letters)
535 of the Arabs [1140/1141 AD],
which is the year
1452 of the Greeks [1140/1141 AD]:
In the First Tishrin the Turks of Melitene entered the monasteries of Bet Zabar,
which are Bet Qanya,
and took plunder and departed.
And in Iyyar the Franks came to seek revenge,
and reached Zopatra and 'Arqa,
and carried off the cattle of the Christians;
while on both sides the Christians were being plundered.
And again the Franks entered the region of Albistan,
and plundered the possessions of the Christians,
and killed a multitude of Turks,
and bound their children and their women.
And at that very time the Turks went out from the region of Hanzit to invade the region of the Franks,
and they encountered the holy bishop of Qalisura as he was crossing Mount Abdahar;
and they seized him and bound him and those who were with him, to kill them.
And suddenly dread of the Franks fell upon them,
and they left them and fled.
And the Franks came and released their prisoners.
And John, emperor of the Greeks, set out,
and reached as far as Neocaesarea.
And the camps of the Greeks and of the Turks remained encamped opposite one another for six months,
and they dispersed without a battle.
